summary: The prepared base reproduced the reported malformed Direct-JSON and XML DSML argument wrappers in both one-shot and streaming parsing. At the exact candidate commit, the focused regression suite, the broader function-call parser suite, and independent adversarial cases all passed. The candidate changes the actual DeepSeekV32 implementation inherited by DeepSeekV4 and preserves legitimate schema properties named input/arguments and ambiguous scalar wrappers. This is a full parser-level fix for the concrete malformed shapes in the original issue, not test-only hardening.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction of nested Direct-JSON wrapper, scalar Direct-JSON wrapper, XML string wrapper, and streaming accumulation. Result: 3 failed, 1 passed.
Candidate regression coverage on the exact SHA, including V3.2/V4 one-shot and streaming wrapper normalization and preservation cases. Result: 10 passed.

Independent cases for every direct-JSON split boundary, bytewise XML streaming, double-encoded dicts, Unicode scalar values, mixed parallel calls, legitimate reserved-name properties, and ambiguous multi-property scalar preservation. Result: 8 passed.
Broader function-call parser regression suite. Result: 253 passed and 4 subtests passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: A numerical sanity check ran on AMD Instinct MI350X with PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 / HIP 7.2 and matched an independent CPU reference exactly. The parser tests themselves are CPU-only.

remaining_limitations: No live DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp server/model was available, so the long-context stochastic generation scenario and OpenAI HTTP transport were not replayed end to end.
The defect and candidate are Python parser-only; no C++/FlyDSL/native source changed, repository-environment.json declares native null, and no native rebuild or compiler/ISA claim was applicable.
GPU architecture is AMD Instinct MI350X (ROCm 7.2); GPU execution was unrelated to the deterministic parser verification.
